the presence of Cl in the catalyst formulation allows the redispersion of Pt to be extended to temperatures above 500 8 C and to higher levels of redispersion, and that this redispersion can be achieved in a continuous fashion, even under reductive conditions.
the redispersion of Pt particles can be achieved at high temperature in the absence of oxygen and in the presence of a reducing agent (CO) in a Pt/Al2 0 3 catalyst system.
the presence of a high concentration of Cl in the catalyst formulation can allow the use of a much lower temperature and a more continuous redispersion of Pt particles in a TWC.

the development of a new and highly innovative approach to the regeneration of spent Pt-based TWCs that can be used “on board” and in situ.
developing an alternative, “in situ” redispersion approach for the regeneration of Pt-based catalysts that can be utilized in the context of exhaust gas treatment.
the development and understanding of a new redispersion process for Pt-based exhaust catalysts.

the oxidative redispersion of Pt/Al2 O 3 by oxygen is not possible in the absence of chlorine and that the use of chlorine is not possible in a TWC application.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated a novel approach for in situ redispersion and rejuvenation of the Pt component of TWCs, and we have shown that this approach can be applied to the Pt/Al2 0 3 system.

the redispersion of the Pt component in a Pt/Al2 O3 catalyst can be accomplished by a combination of the following: (1) the addition of Cl, (2) the use of an oxidizing agent, and (3) a suitable temperature regime.

we have shown the possibility of in situ redispersion and the reactivation of Pt catalysts in exhaust gas environments, without the use of Cl, by using a combination of two techniques: 1) a high-temperature, high-pressure flow reactor system that allows the rapid and controlled switching of the composition of the gas stream and 2) the use of an advanced in situ characterization technique, X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the redispersion of Pt catalysts is possible under conditions that are much more closely representative of those experienced by TWCs in exhausts.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of a novel approach to catalyst regeneration, based on the in-situ redispersion of Pt particles.

it is now possible to achieve redispersion of a supported Pt catalyst in situ, without any need for the presence of Cl, and without the requirement for a specific support material or the use of a particular exhaust composition.
